rules.title: Process running from a user-writable location
rules.description: The process executable path is under a temp, public, downloads or recycle-bin directory. Malware often runs from such locations, but installers and portable tools legitimately do too.
false_positives: Installers, updaters, portable tools and software run from Downloads or Temp.
next_steps: Identify the parent process and the logon session that started it.
Hash and signature-check the file (never run it) and compare with trusted sources.
Correlate the start time with authentication and persistence artifacts.

rules.title: Unsigned or untrusted executable in a user-writable location
rules.description: Authenticode status is NotSigned/HashMismatch/NotTrusted AND the file lives in a user-writable location. Signing status alone is not a verdict: many legitimate tools are unsigned.
false_positives: Internal tools, scripts compiled to executables and developer builds are commonly unsigned.
next_steps: Establish provenance (download source, installer, creation time).
Check the SHA-256 against your IOC list and trusted sources.

rules.title: Office application spawned a script interpreter or proxy-execution binary
rules.description: A document-handling application is the parent of a shell, script host or common proxy-execution binary.
false_positives: Macros and add-ins in managed environments can legitimately launch helpers (rare).
next_steps: Retrieve the document/e-mail that preceded this process and inspect it in isolation.
Review child processes and network connections of the spawned process.

rules.title: PowerShell started with an encoded command
rules.description: PowerShell command line contains -EncodedCommand (or a prefix) with a long Base64-like argument.
rules.why: {name} (pid {pid}) was started with an encoded command.
false_positives: Management agents and installers sometimes pass encoded commands.
next_steps: Decode the Base64 argument offline (UTF-16LE) and review it; do not execute it.
Check PowerShell script-block logs (event 4104) for the same time.

rules.title: Command line contains analyst-defined suspicious pattern
rules.description: Download cradles, hidden windows or LOLBin download switches appear in the (redacted) command line. Edit the list to suit your environment.
rules.why: Process {name} (pid {pid}) command line matches a configured pattern: {cmdline}
false_positives: Administration scripts and deployment tools use these constructs.
next_steps: Identify the parent chain and the user.
Review network connections owned by the pid.
